planning_scheme.name: Sunshine Coast Planning Scheme 2014
planning_scheme.version: Version 27 incorporating Sunshine Coast Planning Scheme (Major Amendment) No. 27 - Site Specific and Editorial Matters (Appendix 2 Table AP2.1); code PDF footers read 'Amended 23 January 2024'
planning_scheme.notes: The scheme commenced on 21 May 2014 (Citation and commencement: 'The commencement date for the planning scheme was 21 May 2014.'). The latest adopted amendment is No. 27 (adopted 27 July 2023, effective 23 January 2024). Neither the adopted-amendments page nor Appendix 2 lists anything later as at October 2026 (the web page was last updated 29 Sep 2026). The proposed NEW Sunshine Coast Planning Scheme was on public notification from 15 Jul to 19 Sep 2025 and is still at the submissions review / final State approval stage. Council's FAQ says: 'It is difficult to predict with any certainty how long these steps will take.' No commencement date was found, so the 2014 scheme remains in force at October 2026. TLPIs in effect: TLPI 01/2025 Accommodation Hotel Incentive Measures (from 4 Apr 2025) and TLPI 04/2025 Kawana Waters Town Centre (from 13 Apr 2026, affects DCP 1 Kawana Waters); neither targets dwelling house siting. State Priority Development Areas (e.g. Caloundra South/Aura, Maroochydore City Centre) and DCP 1 Kawana Waters (Part 10) have their own controls, which are not captured here.

qdc_qhc_relationship.summary: Part 1 s1.6 / Table 1.6.1 says the Dwelling house code (s9.3.6) contains (i) alternative provisions to the QDC for boundary clearance (setback) and site cover for a dwelling house or a class 10 building/structure on the same lot, (ii) provisions about QDC MP1.1/1.2 performance criteria 4 and 8, and (iii) amenity and aesthetics provisions. Within the code, these AOs are tagged 'alternative provision to QDC': AO2.1(a) (6 m road setback for garages/carports/sheds in residential zones), AO3 (house road setback: 4.5 m ground storey / 6 m upper storeys), AO4.1 and AO4.2 (rural/RR/LDLR road setbacks), AO5.1 and AO5.2 (rural/RR/LDLR side and rear setbacks), AO6 (4.5 m canal setback), AO17 (Buderim, Gloucester Rd 10 m) and AO18 (Caloundra LPP-2, 6 m primary frontage). Residential zones have NO side/rear setback or site cover provisions, so QDC/QHC Part 1.1/1.2 values govern those. A dwelling house (including outbuildings) is accepted development subject to the Dwelling house code in the LDR, MDR, RR and LDLR zones. The scheme has NOT been amended to refer to the Queensland Housing Code (there is no amendment after No. 27), and council's sheds page (updated 29 Sep 2026) still cites QDC MP1.1/MP1.2. State transitional provisions (Building and Other Legislation Amendment Regulation 2026, SL 2026 No. 115) reportedly keep the former Building Regulation provisions applying to planning schemes until a scheme is amended or 1 Sept 2029. This was read only through a summarising tool and is NOT verified verbatim.

definitions.text: For a building or structure, the shortest distance measured horizontally from the outermost projection of a building or structure to the vertical projection of the boundary of the lot.

The proportion of the site covered by a building(s), structure(s) attached to the building(s) and carport(s), calculated to the outer most projections of the building(s) and is expressed as a percentage. The term does not include:- (a) any structure or part thereof included in a landscaped open space area such as a gazebo or shade structure; (b) basement car parking areas located wholly below ground level; (c) eaves and sun shading devices.

Means:- (a) if specified in metres--the vertical distance between the ground level and the highest point of the building roof (apex) or parapet at any point, but not including any load bearing antenna, aerial, chimney, flagpole or the like; (b) if specified in storeys--the number of storeys above ground level; or (c) if specified in both metres and storeys, both (a) and (b) apply. Note--Notwithstanding the definition of ground level, for the purpose of determining building height in Precinct CAL LPP-4 (Moffat Beach/Shelly Beach/Dicky Beach), ground level is the level of the land at the time the original estate was subdivided and roads created as determined by a cadastral surveyor, or if this level is not known, the natural level of the ground or probable natural level of the ground as determined by a cadastral surveyor.
The level of the natural ground, or, where the level of the natural ground has been changed, the level as lawfully changed.
Any boundary line, or part thereof, of a lot which coincides with the alignment of a road.

A space that is situated between one floor level and the floor level next above, or if there is no floor above, the ceiling or roof above, but not a space that contains only:- (a) a lift shaft, stairway or meter room; (b) a bathroom, shower room, laundry, water closet, or other sanitary compartment; or (c) a combination of the above. A mezzanine is a storey. A roofed structure on or part of a rooftop that does not solely accommodate building plant and equipment is a storey. A basement is not a storey.
A space that is situated between one floor level and the floor level next below where no part of the space projects more than one metre above ground level.

A residential use of premises for one household that contains a single dwelling. The use includes out-buildings and works normally associated with a dwelling house and may include a secondary dwelling.

Editor's note--in accordance with Schedule 1 (Definitions), a reference to a `dwelling house' in the planning scheme includes a reference to any secondary dwelling or home office associated with the dwelling house, and all outbuildings, structures and works normally associated with a dwelling house.
Means each of the following zones:- (a) Low density residential zone; (b) Medium density residential zone; (c) High density residential zone; and (d) Tourist accommodation zone.

A dwelling used in conjunction with, and subordinate to, a dwelling house on the same lot. A secondary dwelling may be constructed under a dwelling house, be attached to a dwelling house or be freestanding.

An alteration, addition or extension to an existing building(s):- (a) which results in an increase in the gross floor area, of the building(s) of less than five per cent of the gross floor area of the existing building(s) or 50m², whichever is the lesser; and (b) where the building work does not intrude into any boundary setback specified as an acceptable solution in an applicable use code.

local_plan_mechanism.summary: Local plan codes (Part 7) apply only to assessable development. For dwelling houses, local-plan-specific siting rules are written directly into the Dwelling house code under 'Additional Requirements for Dwelling Houses in Certain Areas and Precincts' (PO16-PO19: Blackall Range, Buderim BUD LPP-1, Caloundra CAL LPP-2), and some are tagged as alternative provisions to the QDC. Local plan categories of assessment (s5.9) override zone categories (s5.3.2(8)), but none of those checked changes the assessment of a dwelling house. Structure plans and approved plans of development can also vary dwelling house requirements (9.3.6 footnote 4).

open_questions: The mapped maximum heights (Height of Buildings and Structures Overlay Maps, Schedule 2) were not fetched because the maps are JavaScript/image only. The 8.5 m commonly cited for low density areas is UNVERIFIED; the only mention found is on a council web page, for rural zones.
Whether the AO2.1(c) 56 m2 'total floor area' applies per structure or to all garages, carports and sheds on the lot combined.
Which area PO19/AO19 (secondary dwelling, 45 m2 / 4 m) applies to: it appears under the CAL LPP-2 heading.

The scheme has not yet been amended to reference the Queensland Housing Code. The State transitional provisions (SL 2026 No. 115) need to be confirmed verbatim, specifically how the 'alternative provision to QDC' notes map to QHC Part 1.1/1.2 until 1 Sept 2029.

Pool setbacks: the scheme has no pool provision for residential lots apart from the AO6 canal setback (structures over 1 m) and coastal overlay AO1. Pool siting otherwise follows the QHC / Building Regulation.
Plans of development and structure plans (Palmview, Kawana DCP 1, State PDAs such as Caloundra South) may set different siting rules; these are not covered.
The Low and Medium density residential zone codes contain only purpose and overall outcomes, with no numeric siting AOs. The High density and Tourist accommodation zones were not checked in depth.
Mapped Height of Buildings and Structures Overlay value for EC land is not verified (maps are JavaScript only). It is commonly 8.5 m, but this needs a map/ePlan check per site.

Lots in EC created under a variation approval or approved plan of development (including Palmview) may have POD-specific setbacks and site cover (Dwelling house code footnote 4). These are not in the scheme text and are not alternative provisions under Table 1.6.1. The tool should flag 'check approved plan of development' for EC lots.

Palmview: only the Mixed Density and Medium Density Residential precinct tables list a dwelling house. Other precincts were not checked for dwelling houses beyond a text search. AO24 (20 m from the SEQwater bulk pipeline, OPM P4) has no 's' suffix, so it is not an accepted-development requirement, but it may matter for code assessment.
Whether any EC land lies in the Blackall Range local plan area (AO16.1/AO16.2) or a canal/waterbody area was not checked.

QDC vs QHC: the scheme is unamended since No. 27, so it still refers to QDC MP1.1/1.2. The State transitional position (SL 2026 No. 115) is unverified verbatim (see sunshine_coast.json qdc_qhc_relationship).
State PDAs within or adjoining EC (e.g. Caloundra South / Aura, Beerwah East) are outside the planning scheme and were not covered.
